research_question: In adults with active systemic lupus erythematosus, does belimumab at the standard approved dose (10 mg/kg intravenously, or the equivalent approved 200 mg subcutaneous regimen when used in the trial), compared with placebo, increase the proportion of participants achieving at least a 4-point reduction from baseline in SELENA-SLEDAI score at 52 weeks?
treatment_label: Belimumab at the approved dose (10 mg/kg intravenous or 200 mg subcutaneous) plus background standard therapy
outcome_description: Exact dichotomous endpoint of at least a 4-point reduction from baseline in SELENA-SLEDAI at 52 weeks, extracting the number of participants achieving the reduction and the total number assessed or randomized per eligible arm. In multi-dose studies, include only the belimumab 10 mg/kg arm and the concurrent placebo arm; include belimumab 200 mg subcutaneous when that is the trial regimen. Do not substitute SLE Responder Index, continuous SELENA-SLEDAI change, BILAG, physician global assessment, quality of life, glucocorticoid reduction, adverse events, infections, withdrawals, or mortality.
positive_direction: An RR greater than 1 indicates that more participants achieved a ≥4-point SELENA-SLEDAI reduction at 52 weeks with approved-dose belimumab than with placebo.
search_queries: belimumab placebo randomized trial SELENA-SLEDAI 4 point week 52
belimumab 10 mg/kg controlled SLE SELENA-SLEDAI response
belimumab 200 mg subcutaneous placebo trial SELENA-SLEDAI reduction
inclusion_criteria: Original randomized controlled trials enrolling adults with active systemic lupus erythematosus and comparing belimumab with placebo, generally on background standard therapy.
Trials evaluating the approved belimumab regimen of 10 mg/kg intravenously or 200 mg subcutaneously; for multi-dose trials, only the 10 mg/kg belimumab arm and concurrent placebo arm are eligible.

Reports providing, directly or through linked publications or supplementary material, quantitative arm-level data for the proportion achieving a ≥4-point reduction from baseline in SELENA-SLEDAI at 52 weeks.
exclusion_criteria: Not an original completed randomized empirical study: exclude systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, opinion pieces, theoretical papers, protocols, and non-randomized studies.

No eligible comparison between approved-dose belimumab and a concurrent placebo control condition, including studies reporting only unapproved-dose arms without usable 10 mg/kg intravenous or 200 mg subcutaneous data.

No quantitative data capable of producing an effect size for the exact dichotomous ≥4-point SELENA-SLEDAI reduction at 52 weeks (event counts and arm totals, or an equivalent recoverable proportion required); do not substitute SRI, continuous SELENA-SLEDAI change, BILAG, physician global assessment, quality of life, glucocorticoid reduction, safety outcomes, withdrawals, or mortality.
Completely unrelated to belimumab treatment in adults with active systemic lupus erythematosus.
moderators_to_extract: Belimumab route and regimen (10 mg/kg intravenous vs 200 mg subcutaneous)
Background standard SLE therapy and permitted concomitant immunosuppression
Risk-of-bias domains, including randomization, allocation concealment, blinding, missing outcome data, and selective reporting
effect_size_note: Pool the exact 52-week responder proportions as risk ratios (RRs), using event counts and total participants for each eligible arm. Use only the 10 mg/kg intravenous arm versus concurrent placebo in multi-dose trials, or the approved 200 mg subcutaneous arm versus placebo when applicable. Keep the participant-analysis denominator definition used by each trial (preferably randomized/intention-to-treat) and document any imputation of nonresponders or missing-data rules. If multiple reports describe the same trial, link them and include the trial only once. Use a random-effects model as the primary synthesis, report 95% confidence intervals and heterogeneity (tau-squared and I-squared), and conduct a fixed-effect sensitivity analysis when feasible. Assess risk of bias with RoB 2 and rate certainty with GRADE; investigate publication bias only if enough independent studies are available.
